question: Should OpenClaw add a target-agent concurrency policy, and if so should it be `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` with both global and target limits enforced together?
rationale: The capability remains missing, but introducing a public config surface and choosing how global, target, parent, and named-lane limits compose are product/API decisions rather than a mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Add target-agent cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and admit a spawn only when both the shared global budget and the selected target agent's budget permit it.

options.title: Unify under named lanes
options.body: Resolve this use case through a broader maintainer-approved lane model shared with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10467, accepting a larger API and runtime design.

options.title: Keep global-only policy
options.body: Decline another config surface and retain prompts or external resource controls as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Add target-agent cap
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and admit a spawn only when both the shared global budget and the selected target agent's budget permit it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the shared concurrency resolver, gateway lane setup, and recent subagent policy changes.
